recreation_brief: 1. Set the slide background to light gray #E8E8E8. 2. Draw a thin red (#AA2222) rectangular frame around the entire slide, just inside its edges, enclosing all content. 3. Place the title at top center (~5-25% of slide height): two lines of large bold sans-serif dark red #AA0000 text, line 1 'Non-Numeric', line 2 'Data Representation'. 4. Place a small yellow #FFFF99 circle at the top-right corner containing '27' in black #000000 text. 5. Draw a white #FFFFFF rounded rectangle with a thin red #AA2222 border in the upper-middle band (~27-68% of slide height, full content width with side margins) to hold the bullets. 6. Inside the box, place bullet 1 with a round bullet marker in black #000000: 'What if the data has a non-numeric representation (e.g. Tennis Playing example)'. 7. Place bullet 2 with a round marker in black #000000: 'Features are nominal (Low/High, Yes/No, Overcast/Rainy/Sunny, etc.)'. 8. Place bullet 3 with a round marker in blue #0000CC: 'Features with only 2 possible values can be represented as 0/1'. 9. Place bullet 4 with a round marker in red #CC0000 italic: 'What about features having more than 2 possible values?'. 10. Place bullet 5 with a round marker: render 'Can't we just' in bold black #000000 followed by 'map Sunny to 0, Overcast to 1, Rainy to 2?' in blue #0000CC italic, underlined. 11. Bottom-left (~72-97% of slide height): draw a legend table of 2 columns x 5 rows (no header row) with pale yellow #FFFFCC cells, thin black #000000 borders, and small black sans-serif text; the 5 rows read 'P | Play', 'N | No Play', 'Out | Outlook', 'T | Temperature', 'R | Humidity'. 12. Bottom-center, left of the arrow (~70-97% height): draw a categorical table of 4 columns x 9 rows (1 header row + 8 data rows); header cells 'Y', 'Out', 'T', 'R'; Y column cells white #FFFFFF with values P, N, N, P, P, P, P, N; Out column cells pink #FF99CC with values Sunny, Sunny, Sunny, Overcast, Overcast, Overcast, Rainy, Rainy; T column cells orange #FFCC99 with values Low, High, High, Low, High, Low, Low, Low; R column cells green #99FF99 with values Yes, Yes, No, Yes, No, No, Yes, No; all table text black #000000. 13. Bottom-center, between the two tables: draw a hollow (outline-only) right-pointing arrow in red #CC3333, indicating the transformation from the categorical table to the numeric table. 14. Bottom-center/right, right of the arrow: draw a numeric table of 4 columns x 9 rows (1 header row + 8 data rows); header cells 'Y', 'Out', 'T', 'R'; Y column cells white #FFFFFF with values 1, 0, 0, 1, 1, 1, 0, 1; Out column cells pink #FF99CC each containing '?' (8 question marks, intentional content, not an animation state); T column cells orange #FFCC99 with values 1, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0 [?]; R column cells green #99FF99 with values 1, 1, 0, 0, 0, 1, 0, 1 [?]; all table text black #000000.

recreation_brief: rewritten as a 14-step ordered checklist with exactly one element placed per step, verbatim text, hex colors, height-band positions, and explicit table dimensions (legend 2x5; both data tables 4 columns x 9 rows including header); bullet 4's red specified as accent #CC0000 and bullet 5's blue as #0000CC.
subtitle_or_header: verified genuinely absent from the source (no subtitle region exists; the two-line title is the only header) and left null rather than inventing content.
